Definition: to course (like a beast of prey); by implication, to seek greedily
BiblicalUsage: Locusts run to and fro, and so do the armies of God. Isaiah says your spoil shall be gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar, as the running to and fro of locusts, and Joel says the locust army shall run to and fro in the city and climb up upon the houses. The psalm gives the word its other side, He satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a longing soul is satisfied by the same God who sends the locusts running, because He feeds the hungry and strips the proud.
